public_rationale: Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's director of Autopilot software, gave a deposition in the Huang case that became public in mid-January 2023. Asked whether anyone on the Autopilot team was a human factors engineer, he said 'I do not know.' He did not recall any training on perception-reaction time and said he 'would have to guess what those words mean.' He also said he was not the person studying human lag time. A senior driverless-car employee appearing unfamiliar with basic human-factors ideas fits Marcus's hedged 'apparently unaware'. The Shroff deposition his embedded tweet cites could not be checked, and this verdict does not rest on it.
limitations: Rests on one senior employee, while the claim says 'some employees'.
The Shroff deposition was not located.
The deposition dates from June 2022; only its publicity fell in 'this week'.
'Unaware of human factors engineering' is read as unfamiliar with its core concepts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Court testimony indicates some fairly senior driverless-car employees were apparently unaware of human factors engineering, which is essential when humans are in the loop.

statement.excerpt: We also discovered from court testimony this week that some reasonably high level employees working on driverless cars were apparently unaware of human factors engineering (an absolute necessity if humans are in the loop).

our_interpretation: Plain reading: deposition testimony made public around mid-January 2023 shows at least one fairly senior Tesla Autopilot employee who seemed unfamiliar with basic human-factors ideas, such as perception-reaction time, driver takeover, and whether the team had human-factors engineers.

The Elluswamy deposition in Huang v. Tesla counts. It was the testimony Hikmet's tweets were circulating that week, and Marcus's 'some employees' is not limited to the Shroff deposition named in the embedded tweet.
The aside that human factors is 'an absolute necessity' is an expert judgment and is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Testimony from a senior Autopilot employee shows he did not know or could not explain core human-factors concepts, or whether the team had human-factors engineers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The testimony shows the employees understood human-factors engineering, or the senior employees named were not unfamiliar with it.
